newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on export, rain outlook.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on export, rain outlook.

text.p: KCBT wheat futures closed lower on a lack of significant export business and forecasts for rainfall this week in key hard red winter wheat growing states, traders said.
"The rains so far have been disappointing but there is more forecast during the next two or three days," one trader said, noting crops in Oklahoma and Kansas were generally "in fine shape."
Cash dealers said rains overnight were less than expected but agreed that additional rainfall was in the outlook which could help boost crop production prospects.
"The last couple of days the market appeared tired on the close and it broke today," a trader said. "The break was of light volume and support in July is between $3.85 and $3.88.
Cargill Investor Services sold 1.2 million bushels of July and Term Commodities sold one half million bushels of July, traders said.
Trading volume was estimated by the KCBT at 28,555 contracts, below the 33,385 traded Tuesday.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 4-3/4 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down 4-3/4 at $4.14 a bushel.
